To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most important factors that predict the access to and use technology in the early childhood classroom are the teacher’s belief in technology’s ability to enhance children’s learning and the availability of the technology.

(1) extrinsic barriers influence teachers’ access to a range
of technologies, (2) positive beliefs in childrens’ learning from technology significantly predict actual use of technology, and (3) the relationship between teachers’ beliefs in childrens’
learning from technology and their use of technology is stronger when teachers are more experienced with technology.

the most important predictors of access and use are: (a) the perceived importance of technology in the classroom; (b) teachers’ beliefs that technology can be used to teach children; (c) the extent to which the school supports technology; (d) the extent to the extent to which teachers have access to technology; (e) teachers’ perceptions of the ease of use; and (f) teachers’ perceptions that technology is fun to use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding and predicting teachers’ use of technology in the classroom.
the adoption and use of technology by teachers.
the adoption and use of technology by early childhood teachers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
technology integration in early childhood education has been found to be a complex and challenging task.

the study has provided new insight into factors that influence technology integration specifically for Early Childhood Educators, a sub group which has not been represented much in the literature on technology in formal education.

the findings of the present study are consistent with those reported by previous researchers in that extrinsic barriers are important predictors of teachers’ access to and actual use of technology in the classroom.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of technology in the classroom is a complex process that is influenced by a number of factors, including teachers' attitudes toward technology and their beliefs about the benefits of technology.
we have found that early childhood educators have access to a range technology and are using technology in their classrooms, but they do so at lower rates than K-12 teachers.

teachers’ beliefs in the value of technology for children are a key predictor of their use of technology, but that access to technology is also important, especially for teachers who have not had the opportunity to learn to use the technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
teachers are willing to adopt new technologies if they are given the opportunity to try them and see that they are effective for teaching young children.

early childhood teachers face many of the same extrinsic barriers as other teachers, but that the personal beliefs of the early childhood educator play a significant role in the actual use of technology in the early education setting. This
teachers’ attitudes toward technology use are a critical predictor of their use of technology with young children.
